chapter: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
title: Last days of 52nd Street: the Onyx Club, road dates and George Shearing's debut
summary: He works the Onyx, tours Baltimore to Cleveland, plays the Royal Roost and a concert where he first hears George Shearing.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I went back with him to New York, and we worked the Onyx Club in New York on 52nd Street, which was really the...

I'm happy that I did it, because these were the last days of 52nd Street. And we played 52nd Street, and then we played Baltimore, we played Detroit, Chicago, Cleveland, and a few other places I don't remember. We spent most of the Fall of 1947 on the road.

In December 1947, we went back to New York and we played somewhere there... Oh, we played a place called the Royal Roost, which was on Broadway. During that time, we got an engagement to play... What's the other hall, other than Carnegie...? Anyway, I can't think of the name of the hall now. But it's a very popular hall in New York. And they had this concert there featuring Billy Eckstine and me as his accompanist. If I remember, on this particular concert was a blind pianist that had just arrived in the United States, in New York, from England. He came on and he played a solo thing, played a solo recital. And his name was George Shearing, which later became a very big name. Then he wound up with the quintet. But that was the first time I'd heard George Shearing.
